newsitem.title: USA: CME hog and pork belly futures end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog and pork belly futures end sharply lower.

text.p: CME hog futures ended lower to sharply lower and pork bellies sharply lower to down the 3.000-cent-a-lb limit on pressure from weak cash markets and lack of followthrough on the early short covering rally.
Hog futures ended 1.375 to 0.050 cent lower with October off most at 55.275 cents a lb after a near limit loss of 1.475 cents early. December finished down 0.750 at 54.200 cents.

Pork bellies closed 1.000 cent down to down the daily limit with thinly traded August at the limit. February ended 1.000 lower at 70.425 cents and both July and August posted new contract lows at 71.850 cents and 71.400, respectively.
Hog futures fell to day's lows late as early short covering interest lacked followthrough and fresh selling developed on continued weak cash markets.
"We had short covering early then reality set in based on cash markets," one trader said.

Pork product values are falling on waning demand and heavy kills and expectations are for some product prices to continue easing seasonally. Loin prices were seen slipping into mid-December as there is no demand until after the holidays, some sources noted. Also, loin prices are high currently and will need to go much lower before sparking interest, they said.
